terms.effect: Reflective but colored by the metal itself. Chrome mirrors the environment; gold warms everything it reflects; copper adds pink warmth. Metallic surfaces create some of the most complex light interactions in photography — reflections, caustics, color bleed onto adjacent surfaces.
pairs: Controlled/studio lighting — metallic surfaces are notoriously difficult to light; controlled environments produce the best results
Dark/moody backgrounds — metal pops against darkness
Product photography — jewelry, watches, hardware, automotive
Complementary color accents — gold against deep blue, chrome against red
conflicts: Flat/even lighting — metallic surfaces look dead without highlights
Bright/cluttered backgrounds — reflections pick up everything
Matte/organic palettes — metallic is inherently synthetic and shiny

terms.name: Translucent / Frosted
terms.what: A surface that transmits light but scatters it — you can see light through it but not clear images. Examples: frosted glass, wax, thin paper, backlit leaves, alabaster, skin lit from behind (subsurface scattering).
terms.effect: Soft internal glow. Light passes through and diffuses, creating a luminous quality from within. The object appears to glow rather than reflect. Reads as delicate, ethereal, organic (when biological), or elegant (when architectural/designed).
pairs: Backlighting — light from behind reveals the translucency
Macro photography — thin materials become luminous at close range
Nature — backlit leaves, petals, ice, thin shells
Soft/warm light — the translucency diffuses and warms light beautifully
Ethereal/dreamlike mood — the inner glow is inherently otherworldly
conflicts: Front lighting — translucency is invisible without backlight
Opaque/heavy materials — can't be translucent
Hard/gritty aesthetic — too delicate
terms.example: Backlit translucent leaves + macro + warm light + shallow depth of field → leaves glowing green-gold from within, veins visible as dark networks, soft bokeh behind, ethereal

terms.name: Transparent / Glass
terms.what: Fully see-through materials — glass, crystal, clear water, clear plastic. Light passes through with minimal scattering. Refracts and bends what's behind it.
terms.effect: Distortion and refraction of background elements. Specular highlights on the surface. Caustic light patterns cast onto surfaces below. The material is defined more by what it does to light passing through it than by its own appearance.
pairs: Hard/directional light — creates caustics and defined highlights
Dark backgrounds — the glass edges and highlights become visible
Product photography — perfume bottles, glassware, drinks
Water as a subject — drops, splashes, surfaces
conflicts: Flat/even light — transparent objects disappear without directional light
Matte/diffused aesthetics — glass is all about sharp light interaction
Subjects that need to be clearly visible — glass distorts what's behind it

terms.name: Skin
terms.what: Human skin as a photographic surface — pores, fine lines, peach fuzz (vellus hair), oil/sweat sheen, freckles, moles, scars, and color variation.
terms.effect: The most scrutinized texture in photography. Hard light reveals every pore and imperfection. Soft light smooths and flatters. Oil/sweat creates specular highlights that read as youthful and healthy (or as unwanted shine, depending on context). Subsurface scattering in backlit skin creates a warm glow (light passing through ears, fingers, thin skin).
pairs: Macro/ECU — pores become landscapes, freckles become features
Soft beauty light — smooths texture, creates flattering satin sheen
Hard editorial light — reveals everything, raw and honest
Warm tones — healthy skin reads warm
Portra film — designed specifically for skin tone rendering
conflicts: Extreme hard light + beauty standards — reveals "flaws" (though editorial embraces this)
Heavy grain — competes with skin texture for detail
Cool/desaturated tones — makes skin look unhealthy

terms.name: Wood
terms.what: Grain patterns, knots, rings, and surface quality of wood — from raw/unfinished to polished/lacquered.
terms.effect: Warm, organic, natural. The grain pattern is always unique. Raw wood reads as rustic, handmade, honest. Polished wood reads as refined, warm luxury. Weathered/aged wood reads as history and character. The color ranges from pale birch to deep walnut.
pairs: Warm lighting — amplifies wood's natural warmth
Rustic/natural mood — raw wood is the material of craft
Food/product styling — wood surfaces as backgrounds
Hard side light — raking light reveals grain texture dramatically
Matte or satin finish — the surface quality changes the read entirely
conflicts: High-tech/futuristic aesthetic — wood is natural and traditional
Cool/clinical tones — fights the warmth
Flat/front light — grain texture disappears without directional light

terms.name: Stone / Rock
terms.what: Granite, marble, slate, sandstone, concrete, limestone — dense, heavy, ancient-feeling materials with varied surface qualities.
terms.effect: Solidity, permanence, weight. Rough stone reads as rugged and natural. Polished marble reads as luxurious and classical. Concrete reads as urban, industrial, modern. Each stone type has a distinct visual character — marble's veining, granite's speckle, slate's layers, sandstone's warmth.
pairs: Hard directional light — reveals surface texture and dimensionality
Architectural subjects — stone is the material of buildings
Minimal compositions — a stone surface as a clean background
Cool/neutral tones — stone is naturally neutral
Product photography — marble and concrete as product surfaces
conflicts: Soft/delicate mood — stone is heavy and permanent
Warm organic textures — stone is cold (marble, granite) or earthy (sandstone)
Lightweight/airy feeling — stone has visual weight

terms.name: Fabric / Textile
terms.what: The spectrum of woven, knitted, and felted materials — each with its own drape, weight, texture, and light interaction.
terms.effect: Depends entirely on the specific textile: **Silk/satin** — fluid drape, soft specular highlights, luxurious **Linen** — visible weave, matte, relaxed, natural **Velvet** — deep, light-absorbing, rich, directional nap **Denim** — sturdy, woven texture, casual, workwear **Leather** — heavy, textured, semi-gloss, rugged or refined **Lace** — intricate, delicate, semi-transparent pattern **Wool/knit** — soft, textured, warm, cozy **Chiffon/organza** — sheer, floating, ethereal
pairs: Fashion photography — fabric IS the subject
Soft directional light — reveals drape and fold
Macro/detail shots — weave patterns become abstract
The mood matching the textile — velvet for luxury, linen for casual, lace for delicacy
conflicts: Mismatched mood — velvet in a casual setting, denim in a formal one (unless deliberately subversive)
Flat/front light — fabric drape needs side light to create shadows in the folds

terms.name: Water
terms.what: As a surface/texture, not a subject — the reflective, refractive, moving qualities of water. Still water, rippled, splashing, droplets, condensation, wet surfaces.
terms.effect: **Still water** — mirror reflections, doubled scene, calm **Rippled** — distorted reflections, movement, shimmer **Splashing** — frozen motion (fast shutter) or streaked motion (slow shutter), energy **Droplets** — macro-scale, refractive, each drop is a tiny lens **Wet surfaces** — adds specular reflection to any surface, darkens colors, adds glossy sheen **Condensation** — intimacy (steamy windows, cold glasses), obscuring detail
pairs: Neon/artificial light + wet streets — reflections multiply light and color (the Blade Runner effect)
Macro + water droplets — each drop becomes a tiny world
Long exposure + flowing water — silky smooth texture
Hard light + wet skin — specular highlights, athletic/dramatic
conflicts: Matte aesthetics — water adds gloss to everything
Dry/arid mood — water changes the texture of every surface it touches
Controlled studio work — water is unpredictable and messy
terms.example: Wet city street + neon signs + night + CineStill 800T → every light source doubled in puddle reflections, halation halos reflected, wet asphalt becomes a mirror of color

terms.name: Chrome / Mirror Finish
terms.what: Maximum reflectivity — a perfect or near-perfect mirror surface. Chrome plating, polished stainless steel, mirrored glass.
terms.effect: The surface disappears — you see only the reflection of the environment. The object's shape is defined by how it distorts the reflected world. Reads as futuristic, industrial, high-end, or sci-fi.
pairs: Controlled environments — reflections pick up EVERYTHING, so the environment must be intentional
Studio/product photography — controlled reflections define the shape
Futuristic/sci-fi aesthetic — chrome is the material of the future
Dark environments with specific light sources — the reflections become graphic
conflicts: Cluttered environments — the chrome reflects the mess
Natural/organic mood — chrome is entirely synthetic
Flat lighting — chrome needs something interesting to reflect

terms.name: Plastic / Acrylic
terms.what: Synthetic polymer surfaces — from matte to glossy, opaque to transparent. Includes acrylic, vinyl, resin, silicone, PVC.
terms.effect: Varies hugely by type, but the common thread is a synthetic quality: too uniform for natural, too smooth for organic. Glossy plastic has a bright, cheap-or-fun quality. Clear acrylic reads as modern and clean. Matte plastic reads as industrial or consumer-tech.
pairs: Pop/commercial aesthetics — plastic is the material of consumer products
Bright saturated colors — plastic takes dye well, colors are uniform and vivid
Y2K / retro-futurism — transparent and colored plastic is a Y2K signature
Product photography — electronics, toys, packaging
conflicts: Luxury/premium — plastic reads as cheap (unless deliberately ironic)
Natural/organic aesthetic — plastic is the opposite of natural
Vintage — plastic is modern (except retro-kitschy contexts)

terms.name: Concrete / Brutalist Surface
terms.what: Raw, unfinished concrete — board-formed (showing wood grain imprint), smooth-poured, or rough-aggregate. The material of Brutalist architecture.
terms.effect: Raw, heavy, urban, imposing. The gray surface absorbs and scatters light, creating a flat but textured backdrop. Board-formed concrete shows the ghost of the wooden forms used to pour it — a texture-within-a-texture. Reads as industrial, institutional, or deliberately austere.
pairs: Brutalist architecture — the material IS Brutalism
Hard/directional light — raking light reveals the texture
Minimal compositions — concrete as a clean but textured background
Cool/desaturated tones — concrete's natural gray reinforces coolness
Fashion/editorial contrast — human warmth against cold concrete
conflicts: Warm/cozy mood — concrete is cold and austere
Natural/organic scenes — concrete is manufactured
Polished/luxury aesthetics — unless brutalist-luxury
terms.example: Raw concrete wall + hard side light + fashion model + desaturated grade → texture revealed in raking light, warm skin against cold surface, industrial-editorial contrast

terms.name: Rust / Patina / Decay
terms.what: Surface degradation — oxidized metal (rust), aged copper (verdigris), peeling paint, cracked plaster, weathered wood. The visible evidence of time and exposure.
terms.effect: Age, character, history, impermanence. Rich warm-orange rust, blue-green verdigris, flaking layers revealing what's underneath. The surface tells a story of time passing. Reads as industrial, post-apocalyptic, wabi-sabi, or authentically aged.
pairs: Warm/directional light — reveals the color and texture depth
Macro detail — the decay patterns are beautiful at close range
Vintage/industrial aesthetics — the material of abandoned spaces
Wabi-sabi philosophy — beauty in imperfection and impermanence
Color accent — rust orange and verdigris green are vivid against neutral surroundings
conflicts: Clean/new aesthetics — decay is the opposite of pristine
Modern/tech — rust signals neglect in a tech context
Sterile/clinical environments — decay is organic and unpredictable

terms.name: Neon / LED Glow
terms.what: Self-luminous surfaces — neon tubes, LED strips, backlit signs, screen glow. Not a texture in the traditional sense, but a surface quality that changes everything around it.
terms.effect: The surface emits light rather than reflecting it. Creates color wash on nearby surfaces. Defines zones of color in the scene. The glow bleeds outward, especially in fog, rain, or on reflective surfaces. Reads as urban, nightlife, futuristic, or cyberpunk.
pairs: Nighttime/low light — neon is most effective in darkness
Wet surfaces — reflections multiply the color
Fog/haze — volumetric glow around the source
Cyberpunk/sci-fi aesthetic — neon is the genre's material
Portraiture — neon as colored key light on the face
conflicts: Natural/organic environments — neon is urban and synthetic
Daytime — neon is invisible in bright ambient light
Warm/natural skin tones — the color cast changes everything

terms.name: Iridescent / Holographic
terms.what: Surfaces that shift color depending on viewing angle (iridescent: soap bubbles, beetle shells, oil slicks) or display rainbow diffraction patterns (holographic: foil, stickers, packaging).
terms.effect: Rainbow color shifts, prismatic reflections, dynamic appearance implying movement even in stills. Reads as futuristic, magical, or precious. Iridescent is organic (pearl, shell); holographic is synthetic (foil, packaging).
pairs: Y2K aesthetic, vaporwave, sci-fi, fashion editorial, dark backgrounds, macro photography.
conflicts: Muted/earthy palettes, matte textures, vintage aesthetics, warm color grading.

terms.name: Pearlescent
terms.what: Soft lustrous sheen with subtle color shift — like the inside of an oyster shell. Less dramatic than iridescent. Shifts mainly between white and one or two soft colors.
terms.effect: Soft glow, elegant, subtle color play, luminous without flashy. Reads as luxury, feminine, delicate.
pairs: Soft lighting, beauty photography, luxury branding, pastel palettes, wedding aesthetics, silk.
conflicts: Harsh contrast, gritty textures, industrial aesthetics, bold saturated color.

terms.name: Brushed Metal
terms.what: Metal finished with fine parallel abrasion lines, creating directional reflection rather than mirror reflection. Common on appliances, watches, industrial design.
terms.effect: Soft directional highlight streaks. Matte-adjacent but clearly metallic. Industrial sophistication. Visible grain and directionality in the surface. Reads as modern, industrial, premium.
pairs: Industrial design, product photography, minimalist aesthetic, cool color temperatures, modern architecture.
conflicts: Organic/natural aesthetics, warm rustic looks, highly polished mirror surfaces.

terms.name: Carbon Fiber
terms.what: Woven carbon filament composite with distinctive visible twill weave pattern. Used in automotive, aerospace, luxury goods.
terms.effect: Dark, almost black with subtle sheen. Visible geometric weave pattern catches light. Reads as high-tech, performance, expensive. The weave creates a subtle moiré-like texture.
pairs: Automotive photography, tech products, dark/moody lighting, red + carbon fiber (classic combo), industrial luxury.
conflicts: Organic/natural subjects, soft/feminine aesthetics, vintage, pastels.

terms.name: Marble (Specific Veining Types)
terms.what: The vein patterns in marble — each type has dramatically different character: **Carrara** — grey veining on white, subtle, classic Italian **Calacatta** — bold gold/grey veining on white, dramatic, expensive-looking **Nero Marquina** — white veining on black, dramatic **Verde Guatemala** — white veining on deep green **Rose marble** — warm pink with grey/white veining
terms.effect: Organic flowing lines, luxury, classical. Each type sets a different mood — Calacatta is bold, Carrara is subtle, Nero Marquina is dramatic.
pairs: Luxury branding, classical architecture, flat lay photography, gold accents, minimalist design.
conflicts: Industrial/tech (usually), rustic/rough textures, busy patterns competing with the veining.

terms.name: Patent leather
terms.effect: high-gloss lacquered mirror finish. Formal, fetish, fashion. Catches highlights sharply.
pairs: Warm lighting, earth tones, period settings, close-up detail shots.

terms.name: Suede
terms.effect: napped, soft, matte. Warm, tactile, casual luxury. Absorbs light.
pairs: Warm lighting, earth tones, period settings, close-up detail shots.

terms.name: Distressed leather
terms.effect: worn, cracked, faded. Rugged, vintage, authentic. Shows use and history.
pairs: Warm lighting, earth tones, period settings, close-up detail shots.

terms.name: Tooled/Embossed
terms.effect: stamped decorative patterns. Western, artisan, ornate.
pairs: Warm lighting, earth tones, period settings, close-up detail shots.

terms.name: Vegetable-tanned
terms.effect: natural tan, ages/patinas over time. Craft, heritage, honest.
pairs: Warm lighting, earth tones, period settings, close-up detail shots.

terms.name: Denim
terms.what: Woven cotton twill with characteristic diagonal ribbing. Varies from raw/rigid (dark, uniform indigo) to heavily distressed (faded, torn, whiskers).
terms.effect: Raw denim reads as sharp/intentional; distressed reads as lived-in/rebellious. Casual, American, workwear heritage. The texture is universally recognizable.
pairs: Americana, street photography, fashion editorial, warm natural light, leather and copper accents.
conflicts: Formal/luxury (unless deliberately subverted), high-tech surfaces, very polished textures.

terms.name: Ceramic / Porcelain
terms.what: Fired clay materials ranging from rough stoneware to ultra-smooth porcelain. **Ceramic** — handmade, warm, slightly imperfect. **Porcelain** — refined, cool, elegant, sometimes translucent. Glazed adds shine; unglazed (bisque) is matte and chalky.
terms.effect: Ceramic reads as artisan, wabi-sabi, craft. Porcelain reads as pristine, cool, luxury. The spectrum from rough to refined spans the entire material.
pairs: Still life, minimalist design, food photography, Japanese aesthetics (wabi-sabi for rough ceramic), luxury branding (fine porcelain).
conflicts: Industrial/tech (for ceramic); rustic/rough (for fine porcelain).

terms.name: Kraft
terms.effect: brown, unbleached, rough. Eco, packaging, rustic, DIY. Visible fiber.
pairs: Typography, letterpress, stationery design, botanical illustration, warm soft lighting.
conflicts: Digital/screen aesthetics, high-gloss finishes, high-tech subjects.

terms.name: Vellum
terms.effect: smooth, translucent, slightly waxy. Classical, archival, precious.
pairs: Typography, letterpress, stationery design, botanical illustration, warm soft lighting.
conflicts: Digital/screen aesthetics, high-gloss finishes, high-tech subjects.

terms.name: Handmade / Deckle edge
terms.effect: irregular edges, visible fiber, uneven surface. Artisan, letterpress, fine art.
pairs: Typography, letterpress, stationery design, botanical illustration, warm soft lighting.
conflicts: Digital/screen aesthetics, high-gloss finishes, high-tech subjects.

terms.name: Japanese washi
terms.effect: translucent, fibrous, delicate. Long visible fibers. Japanese aesthetic, meditation, light-filtering.
pairs: Typography, letterpress, stationery design, botanical illustration, warm soft lighting.
conflicts: Digital/screen aesthetics, high-gloss finishes, high-tech subjects.

terms.name: Cotton rag
terms.effect: thick, textured, archival. Fine art, printmaking, photography printing.
pairs: Typography, letterpress, stationery design, botanical illustration, warm soft lighting.
conflicts: Digital/screen aesthetics, high-gloss finishes, high-tech subjects.

terms.name: Gold leaf
terms.effect: ultra-thin hammered gold, slightly irregular with cracks and overlap seams. Warm, rich, classical luxury.
pairs: Dark backgrounds (black + gold is timeless), jewel tones, typography/lettering, luxury branding, Art Deco.
conflicts: Minimalism (unless very sparse), matte/raw aesthetics, casual/budget looks.

terms.name: Silver leaf
terms.effect: cooler tone, tarnishes darker over time.
pairs: Dark backgrounds (black + gold is timeless), jewel tones, typography/lettering, luxury branding, Art Deco.
conflicts: Minimalism (unless very sparse), matte/raw aesthetics, casual/budget looks.

terms.name: Metallic foil (hot stamp)
terms.effect: machine-applied, more uniform. Modern luxury, packaging, editorial.
pairs: Dark backgrounds (black + gold is timeless), jewel tones, typography/lettering, luxury branding, Art Deco.
conflicts: Minimalism (unless very sparse), matte/raw aesthetics, casual/budget looks.

terms.name: Copper leaf
terms.effect: warm, shifts to verdigris patina. Craft, steampunk, industrial warmth.
pairs: Dark backgrounds (black + gold is timeless), jewel tones, typography/lettering, luxury branding, Art Deco.
conflicts: Minimalism (unless very sparse), matte/raw aesthetics, casual/budget looks.

terms.name: Clear Sky / Direct Sun
terms.what: Cloudless sky, direct unobstructed sunlight. The quality and mood shifts dramatically by time of day (see Time of Day section below).
terms.effect: Hard, defined shadows. High contrast. Strong color saturation in direct light. Blue sky provides cool fill in shadows. The harshest conditions at midday, the most beautiful at golden hour.
pairs: Hard midday sun (high contrast editorial), golden hour (warm romantic), landscape (clear visibility to horizon), architecture (strong shadow patterns).
conflicts: Soft/diffused light (clear sky IS hard light at midday), moody/atmospheric (too much visibility), overcast-dependent aesthetics.

terms.name: Overcast / Cloudy
terms.what: Cloud cover acting as a giant diffuser. The sky becomes one enormous soft light source.
terms.effect: Soft, even, shadowless or near-shadowless illumination. Slightly cool color temperature (~6500K+). Colors appear saturated but without contrast — vivid but flat. Skin looks smooth and even. Reads as contemplative, muted, melancholic, or quietly beautiful.
pairs: Portrait photography (flattering, even), product photography outdoors (accurate color), melancholic mood, muted/desaturated palette, green landscapes (overcast makes foliage vivid), street photography.
conflicts: Dramatic shadow play, warm/golden mood, high-contrast compositions, sun-dependent lighting setups.

terms.name: Rain
terms.what: The single most transformative weather condition for visual work. Rain changes every surface in the frame — asphalt becomes a mirror, skin glistens, glass distorts, neon signs double in puddles.
terms.effect: **Wet surfaces become reflective** — this is rain's primary visual gift. Every surface gains specular quality. Puddles create mirror reflections of light sources. Pavement doubles neon signs, streetlights, and headlights. The air itself becomes visible (falling rain catches light). Clothing clings. Hair becomes textured. Overcast sky provides soft ambient, but artificial lights punch through dramatically.
pairs: Neon/artificial lighting — reflections in wet surfaces multiply every light source (the Blade Runner effect)
Cyberpunk — rain is the genre's native weather
Film noir — rain-slicked streets are the signature
Wong Kar-wai — wet glass, neon reflections, romantic melancholy
Night scenes — rain + darkness + artificial light = maximum atmosphere
CineStill 800T — halation on rain-reflected lights
Direct flash — flash catching individual raindrops mid-fall
conflicts: Dry/arid aesthetics, bright/airy mood, clear sharp backgrounds (rain adds haze), cottagecore (unless gentle spring rain).
terms.example: Night rain + neon signs + wet street reflections + anamorphic lens flares + shallow DOF → every light source doubled in puddles, blue and pink streaks from neon, rain catching backlight, cinematic atmosphere

terms.name: Snow
terms.what: Falling and accumulated snow. White ground cover acts as a giant reflector bouncing light upward (under-lighting). Falling snowflakes catch light.
terms.effect: **High-key natural environment** — the white ground raises the ambient light level. Fill light from below (reflected off snow) softens shadows under chin and brow. Falling snow adds particle texture to the air. Color palette shifts cool — blue shadows on white snow. Accumulated snow simplifies the landscape (hides detail, creates clean white shapes). Reads as quiet, clean, isolated, magical, or cold depending on context.
pairs: Cool/blue color grade, high-key natural, quiet/contemplative mood, isolation (tracks in fresh snow), holiday/winter warmth (warm interior light against cold exterior), shallow DOF (snowflakes become bokeh), backlit falling snow (each flake glows).
conflicts: Warm/tropical, saturated warm color, green/lush landscapes, summer aesthetics.
terms.example: Falling snow + backlit by streetlight + warm tungsten window glow + figure in dark coat + shallow DOF → snowflakes glowing as bokeh in foreground, warm/cool contrast between interior and exterior, quiet and magical

terms.name: Mist / Light Rain / Drizzle
terms.what: Fine moisture in the air — between fog and rain. Surfaces are damp but not flowing. The air has a slight veil.
terms.effect: Subtle atmospheric softening. Surfaces are damp (slight sheen) but not mirror-wet like heavy rain. Air has a faint haze. Colors are slightly muted. Reads as gentle, dreamy, British/Pacific Northwest, literary.
pairs: Overcast sky, muted palette, green landscapes (lush and wet), literary mood, Saul Leiter (shooting through wet glass), cottagecore (gentle spring rain).

terms.name: Fog / Heavy Mist
terms.what: Dense moisture in the air reducing visibility. Objects fade with distance. The air itself becomes a visible medium.
terms.effect: **Atmospheric perspective at extreme** — objects lose contrast and detail with distance, fading to gray/white. Near objects are sharp, mid-ground softens, far objects are silhouettes or invisible. Depth layers become obvious. Light sources get halos and bloom. Reads as mysterious, isolated, eerie, dreamlike, or cinematic.
pairs: Rim light / backlight — light catches fog from behind, creating volumetric god rays
Horror / mystery — obscured visibility creates tension
Silhouettes — figures emerge from or disappear into fog
Film noir — fog + streetlight = atmospheric crime scene
Long focal length — telephoto compression through fog layers
Landscape — depth layers revealed by fog filling valleys
conflicts: Full visibility (fog removes it), crisp detail at distance, bright sunny conditions (fog burns off in sun).
terms.example: Dense fog + single streetlight + figure approaching + rim-lit from behind → silhouette emerging from white void, volumetric light rays, depth completely obscured, noir mystery

terms.name: Haze / Smog
terms.what: Lighter than fog — a subtle atmospheric veil that reduces contrast at distance without obscuring visibility. Urban smog, summer heat haze, wildfire smoke.
terms.effect: Slightly reduced contrast globally. Warm-tinted (smog) or neutral (haze). Distant objects soften but remain visible. The atmosphere has weight. Reads as hot, urban, polluted, or dreamy depending on context.
pairs: Golden hour (haze amplifies warm color), urban landscapes (city haze is a real phenomenon), telephoto compression (amplified by atmospheric layers), vintage/retro (older photos had more atmospheric haze), Apocalypse Now aesthetic (jungle haze + fire).
conflicts: Crisp clear air, high-contrast photography, cool/blue palette (haze is warm).

terms.name: Dust / Sand
terms.what: Airborne particulates — dust storms, desert wind, construction sites, dirt roads. Visible particles in the air.
terms.effect: Warm amber/golden atmospheric veil. Hard backlighting catches individual particles — the air sparkles. Surfaces accumulate dust (matte quality). Reduced visibility in heavy dust. Reads as hot, rugged, frontier, apocalyptic, or earthy.
pairs: Western/desert aesthetics, golden hour (dust + warm light = golden atmosphere), practical lighting (headlights through dust), Mad Max/post-apocalyptic, military, construction/industrial, hard backlight (every particle catches light).
conflicts: Clean/pristine, clinical, urban (unless construction context), cool palettes.

terms.name: Smoke
terms.what: Visible combustion product in the air — from fires, cigarettes, machines, fog machines. Thicker and more defined than haze, catches light dramatically.
terms.effect: **Volumetric light becomes visible** — any beam of light passing through smoke creates a visible shaft (god rays). Smoke drifts and curls, creating organic movement. Warm-tinted if from fire, neutral if theatrical. Reads as dramatic, cinematic, dangerous, atmospheric.
pairs: Hard directional light — creates visible beams through smoke
Fire/ember particles — smoke + fire is natural
Film noir — cigarette smoke in a beam of light
Concert/stage lighting — theatrical haze
Chiaroscuro — smoke makes the light sculptural
Blade Runner — smoke + neon + rain = the trinity
conflicts: Clean/clinical, bright/airy, outdoor/natural (unless campfire or wildfire).

terms.name: Steam / Vapor
terms.what: Water vapor — from hot food, hot surfaces in rain, bathroom, industrial vents, manholes in cold cities.
terms.effect: Soft, warm, rising. Lighter and more translucent than smoke. Catches backlight beautifully. Rising steam from hot food signals freshness and temperature. Street steam (NYC manholes) adds urban atmosphere. Reads as warm, fresh, urban, or industrial.
pairs: Food photography (steam = hot and fresh), hot beverage (rising steam from coffee), urban night (manhole steam + streetlight), backlight (steam glows), bathroom/sauna (intimate, warm).

terms.name: Dawn / First Light
terms.effect: Deep blue sky transitioning to warm horizon. Extremely soft, directional. Cool overall with warm edge where sun is about to rise. Long shadows. Quiet, fresh, untouched. Almost no one is awake.
pairs: Landscape, solitude, new beginnings, running/exercise, mist on water, birds.

extras.Color temperature: ~4000-5000K, shifting warm as sun nears horizon.

terms.name: Early Morning (7-9am)
terms.effect: Low warm sun, long golden shadows, clean air (no midday haze). Similar to golden hour but the world is waking up, not winding down — the mood is fresh and forward-looking rather than nostalgic.
pairs: Lifestyle photography, jogging/health, coffee, commute, dewy surfaces, fresh light.

terms.name: Midday (11am-1pm)
terms.effect: Sun directly overhead. Short, hard shadows directly below subjects. Harsh, unflattering on faces (deep eye socket shadows). Maximum contrast. Maximum color saturation in direct sun. Blue fill in shadows from open sky. The "worst" light for conventional portraits but powerful for graphic/editorial work.
pairs: Hard editorial fashion, graphic shadow patterns, saturated color, harsh texture reveal, street photography (high contrast urban), documentary (unflinching).
conflicts: Flattering portraiture, soft/romantic, golden hour warmth.

terms.name: Afternoon (2-4pm)
terms.effect: Sun lowering but still relatively high. Warm light from the side. Shadows lengthening. The transition period — warmer than midday but not yet golden hour. Common for event photography, outdoor weddings, lifestyle.
pairs: Lifestyle, outdoor events, warm natural, environmental portraits.

terms.name: Golden Hour (last hour before sunset)
terms.effect: See lighting.md for full entry. Warm (~3500K), soft, directional, long shadows, gentle contrast, everything glows. The most universally flattering natural light.

terms.name: Sunset
terms.effect: The dramatic moment. Vivid orange/red/purple sky. Sun at horizon — subjects can be backlit (silhouette) or front-lit (last warm light on face). The sky becomes the subject. Maximum color in the atmosphere.
pairs: Silhouettes, vivid sky, romantic, dramatic, wide angle (maximize sky), epic landscape.

terms.name: Blue Hour (20-40 min after sunset)
terms.effect: See lighting.md for full entry. Deep saturated blue sky. Artificial lights (warm) against blue sky (cool) — natural complementary contrast. The color of twilight.

terms.name: Night
terms.effect: No natural ambient. All light is artificial — streetlights, neon, headlights, windows, practicals. High contrast between lit and unlit areas. The darkness itself is a compositional element. Color is determined entirely by the artificial sources.
pairs: Neon, cyberpunk, film noir, CineStill 800T, long exposure (light trails), urban, mystery, horror, nightlife.
conflicts: Natural light, golden hour, high-key, bright/airy.

terms.name: Deep Night / 3am
terms.effect: Minimal artificial light. Near-total darkness with isolated pools of illumination — a single streetlight, a vending machine, a phone screen. The emptiness is the content. Reads as liminal, lonely, insomniac, contemplative, eerie.
pairs: Liminal space aesthetic, noir, horror, isolation, long exposure, available light only, Crewdson suburban uncanny.

terms.name: Melancholic
terms.effect: Desaturated palette, cool blue/gray tones, overcast or blue hour light, negative space, isolated subject, shallow DOF (subject sharp, world blurred), slight film grain, muted color, long shadows or flat light.

terms.name: Energetic
terms.effect: High saturation, warm or vivid complementary colors, diagonal composition, tight crop, direct flash or hard light, motion blur or speed lines, low angle (power), wide angle (distortion/dynamism).

terms.name: Intimate
terms.effect: Shallow DOF (f/1.4-f/2), warm color (tungsten/candlelight), close framing (MCU or CU), soft directional light (window), visible grain, practical lighting, quiet negative space around the subject.

terms.name: Ominous / Dread
terms.effect: Low-key lighting, under-lighting or top-lighting (unnatural shadow direction), cool desaturated with one warm accent, fog or haze, wide angle for distortion, low angle looking up, crushed blacks, liminal space, deep night.

terms.name: Nostalgic
terms.effect: Warm vintage grade (lifted blacks, amber tint), film grain (Portra 400 or Kodak Gold), soft overexposed highlights, golden hour, slightly faded saturation, vignetting, medium format (rich tonality), subjects looking away from camera.

terms.name: Serene / Peaceful
terms.effect: Soft diffused light (overcast or open shade), analogous cool or warm palette, wide shot with negative space, deep DOF (everything sharp and equal), horizontal composition, symmetry or balanced framing, gentle natural environment.

terms.name: Chaotic
terms.effect: Dutch angle, multiple competing light sources (mixed color temperature), tight crop with elements exiting frame, high saturation clashing colors, motion blur, grain, direct flash, wide angle distortion, busy composition, no negative space.

terms.name: Luxurious
terms.effect: Medium format or large format (rich tonality), soft directional light with specular highlights, warm gold/amber, shallow DOF, glossy/reflective surfaces, dark background, negative space, precise composition, beauty dish or clamshell lighting.

terms.name: Eerie / Uncanny
terms.effect: Slightly wrong lighting (motivated from an unusual source), desaturated with one oversaturated element, liminal space, deep focus (everything sharp — nothing escapes attention), slight dutch angle, overcast or fluorescent, subjects slightly off-center, empty architecture.

terms.name: Joyful
terms.effect: High-key, bright warm light (golden hour or overcast + warm grade), high saturation, wide smile/expression, wide angle for expansive feeling, vivid color accents, motion/action, slightly overexposed, candid/unposed framing.
